mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth combined with low federal funds rate indicates a supportive environment for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth and low Fed Funds but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production in a late-cycle expansion signals potential inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of late-cycle cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing non-farm payroll employment suggests economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate above 4% tightens monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation and low unemployment signal tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rises and UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts in a post-shock recovery indicate economic rebound, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of post-shock cases.
